windows: Download WireGuard for Windows from https://www.wireguard.com/install/ and install it.
In the app, click "Add Tunnel" → "Import from file".
macos: Install WireGuard from the Mac App Store (or https://www.wireguard.com/install/).
"Import tunnel(s) from file" → pick the downloaded .conf.
linux_nm: NetworkManager 1.16 and newer supports WireGuard natively.
KDE Plasma: Connection settings (or nm-applet) → "Add VPN" → "Import from file".
linux_cli: One-off start: sudo wg-quick up wg0.
Start on boot: sudo systemctl enable --now wg-quick@wg0.
ios: Install WireGuard from the App Store.
Tap "+" → "Create from QR code" and scan the QR (from another screen).
Or "+" → "Import from file/archive" if the config was downloaded as a file.
android: Install WireGuard from Google Play (or F-Droid).
Tap "+" → scan the QR code, or import the .conf file.

amneziawg.appNote: Important: the regular WireGuard app does not understand the obfuscation fields (Jc/Jmin/Jmax/S1/S2/H1-4) — you need an AmneziaWG-aware client: the Amnezia VPN app (amnezia.org) or the amneziawg-tools package on Linux.
windows: Import the downloaded .conf — the obfuscation fields come along automatically.
linux_nm: NetworkManager doesn't natively understand AmneziaWG's obfuscation fields.
Use the Amnezia VPN app if a build exists for your distro.
Otherwise switch to the "Command line" tab.
linux_cli: Install amneziawg-tools — a wireguard-tools fork with obfuscation support.
One-off start: sudo awg-quick up awg0.
Start on boot: sudo systemctl enable --now awg-quick@awg0.
ios: Install Amnezia VPN from the App Store.
android: Install Amnezia VPN from Google Play.

openvpn.appNote: Official client — works the same way on every platform.
windows: Download OpenVPN Connect from https://openvpn.net/client/ and install it.
Import the downloaded .ovpn (Import Profile → From file), or just open the file directly and the app will pick it up.
macos: Download OpenVPN Connect from https://openvpn.net/client/ (or the Mac App Store).
linux_nm: Make sure the network-manager-openvpn plugin is installed (usually already present on Ubuntu/Fedora).
Network Settings → "Add VPN" → "Import a saved VPN configuration".
linux_cli: As a service: place the file at /etc/openvpn/client/client.conf, then sudo systemctl enable --now openvpn-client@client.
ios: Download OpenVPN Connect from the App Store.
Open the downloaded .ovpn file (e.g. shared from Mail/Files) — the app will offer to import it.
android: Download OpenVPN Connect from Google Play.
Open the downloaded .ovpn file — the app will offer to import it.

ikev2.appNote: Windows/macOS/iOS use the system's own VPN client — no third-party app needed, but the issued .p12 certificate must be installed first. Android/Linux need a separate app.
windows: Double-click the downloaded .p12 file and install the certificate (enter the issued password).
Settings → Network → VPN → "Add a VPN connection".
Connection type — IKEv2, enter the server address.
macos: Easiest: open the provided .mobileconfig — the VPN profile configures itself automatically, including the certificate.
Manually: System Settings → Network → "+" → type IKEv2.
linux_nm: Install the network-manager-strongswan plugin if available for your distro.
Network Settings → "Add VPN" → strongSwan → enter the server and import the .p12.
linux_cli: Steps vary by strongSwan version — see strongswan.org's documentation.
ios: Open the provided .mobileconfig directly on the device (via Mail/AirDrop/Files).
The certificate and VPN profile are configured automatically.
android: Install the strongSwan VPN Client from Google Play.
In the app, import the .p12 certificate (with the issued password).
Add a VPN profile with the server address.
